planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Red Lotus Tree is frost-hardy to about 0°F, more cold-tolerant than most evergreen magnolias.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; Red Lotus Tree (also classified as Manglietia insignis) is an evergreen reaching 25-30 feet, with leathery glossy leaves and fragrant reddish-pink-and-white chalice-shaped flowers that appear in the leaf axils, often blooming even on young plants in late spring. It is reported hardy to roughly 0°F, notably more cold-tolerant than most other evergreen magnolias, making it a good choice for extending evergreen magnolia culture into zone 7.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Japanese Bigleaf Magnolia blooms later than most magnolias, in late May to June.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; Japanese Bigleaf Magnolia (also known by the synonym Magnolia hypoleuca) is a deciduous tree with huge obovate leaves 18-24 inches long, bearing upward-facing, fragrant, creamy-white flowers with red stamens in late May and June, after most other magnolias have finished blooming. Its enormous leaves give it a dramatically bold, almost tropical texture for a cold-hardy deciduous tree, and it is grown both for its late bloom and its striking foliage scale.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; Tamaulipas Magnolia is a heat-tolerant evergreen magnolia, a good warm-climate alternative to the ubiquitous Magnolia grandiflora.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Tamaulipas Magnolia is a heat-tolerant evergreen tree reaching 20-30 feet, native to northeastern Mexico, with glossy leaves showing coppery new growth and fragrant white flowers up to 6 inches across in spring. It makes a good warm-climate alternative to the much larger and more common Magnolia grandiflora, fitting better into a mid-size garden while offering similar evergreen structure and fragrant bloom. It performs especially well in hot, humid Gulf Coast and Texas climates.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in part shade to full sun; Chinese Wood-Lotus shares culture with the related Magnolia insignis.

directions: Plant in part shade to full sun in moist, fertile, well-drained soil; Chinese Wood-Lotus is an evergreen species in the Manglietia/insignis group, bearing leathery dark-green leaves and creamy-white fragrant flowers. Its culture closely mirrors that of the related Magnolia insignis, needing similarly moist, fertile soil and benefiting from some shelter in colder parts of its hardiness range. It is a specialty item sourced mainly through Camellia Forest Nursery and similar collector-focused magnolia specialists.

planting.note: Plant container-grown young trees in spring into moist, well-drained soil in part shade to full sun in a warm, sheltered site; Foveolata is tender and best suited to zone 8-9 only.

directions: Plant in part shade to full sun in moist, well-drained soil in a warm, sheltered site; Foveolata is an evergreen magnolia species from northern Vietnam, notable for genuinely yellow-toned flowers, an unusual color within the genus. It is tender and best suited to zone 8-9 only, needing protection from hard freezes, and is currently sold mainly as young plants by specialty collector nurseries. Its yellow bloom color makes it a genuine rarity worth seeking out for a warm-climate magnolia collection.

planting.note: Plant grafted or container-grown trees in spring into moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; the true straight species takes 20 or more years to first flower, distinct from the faster-flowering var. robusta and 'Blood Moon' selection already in cultivation.

directions: Plant in full sun in moist, fertile, well-drained soil, giving it a spacious, sheltered site protected from late frost. The true Magnolia sargentiana species, native to Sichuan, China, grows into a large deciduous tree 50-60 feet tall, bearing large pale-pink saucer-shaped flowers 8-10 inches across in early spring before the leaves emerge. Most commercial stock sold under this species name is actually the faster-flowering var. robusta or the darker 'Blood Moon' selection already in cultivation, since the true species can take 20 or more years from seed to first bloom, making genuine straight-species nursery stock genuinely rare.
